findings.message: Skill reads from agent configuration directories (.claude/, .codex/, .gemini/). These directories may contain API keys, personal settings, and other credentials that the skill has no legitimate need to access.
findings.remediation: Remove all code or instructions that access agent configuration directories (.claude/, .codex/, .gemini/). If configuration values are needed, pass them explicitly as parameters or environment variables — never read the agent's own config files.

findings.code_snippet: strict form `[cd <dir> &&] git [-C <dir>]... commit|push [<option or name>]...` and git reports another work tree for the target (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel --absolute-git-dir` gives a different top level and a different git directory than for the session directory). For a push, the common git directory must differ too: linked worktrees share refs, so a push from another linked worktree of the session repository audits the session tree and the target. The one exception is a push that cannot send the session branch: the options are only `-u`, `-q`, `--set-upstream`, `--force-with-lease` and `--force-if-includes`, `git rev-parse --symbolic-full-name` gives the checked-out branch of the target for each refspec source, that branch is not the session branch, and a push without a refspec has `push.default` unset or `simple`, `current`, `upstream` or `nothing` and no remote `push` or `mirror` setting. That push audits only the target. A git error during this check keeps the session audit.

Formatters, linters, and checkers are the exception. They read their file arguments but do not run them, so `eslint src/a.ts`, `prettier --check "**/*.ts"`, `oxlint src/`, `biome check`, `stylelint`, `textlint`, and similar tools make no entry points. This applies to the common package-manager and wrapper forms (`npx`, `pnpm exec`, `pnpm --filter web exec`, `pnpm -r exec`, `yarn run`, `cross-env`, `dotenv -e .env --`, `varlock run --`), and to a call of a script that runs the tool (`npm run lint -- src/a.ts`, `npm run lint src/a.ts`, `yarn lint src/a.ts`). The tool stays a used dependency, its `--config` file stays tracked, and a module that it loads through a flag (`eslint -f ./fmt.js`, `prettier --plugin=./plugin.mjs`) stays reachable.

16. **Run `fallow doctor --format json --quiet` as a preflight**. Run it before the first analysis of a project, and again when a result looks wrong (an empty result, many unresolved imports, or missing workspaces). The doctor run reads the project setup and changes nothing. A required check with `status: "fail"` makes it exit 2. Fix each `fail` check before you trust the analysis. A `warn` message names the part of the analysis that degrades; a stale cache only makes the next run slower. Run each `remediation.command` from the project root (`cwd` is `.`). You may run it without asking when its `mutating` field is `false`; such a command can still write the Fallow cache. Ask the user before you run a remediation with `mutating: true`, such as a dependency install.
